title: From Silicon to System | A Journey in Fault Isolation
gist: An EDFAS webinar billing for Dr. Joy Lao, NVIDIA's Senior Manager of System Fault Isolation, tracing 25 years from Texas Instruments failure analysis to pioneering the DFT-EFA methodology at NVIDIA - including dynamic laser stimulation work credited with recovering millions of dollars per month in shipments and the transfer of the DFT-EFA workflow into TSMC's FA lab. The listed agenda flags backside power delivery and FA workforce development as the emerging constraints.

themes.theme: Failure analysis as a revenue lever

insights.claim: Using dynamic laser stimulation on an inherited laser scanning microscope to localize failing transistors is credited with recovering millions of dollars per month in NVIDIA shipments, making fault isolation a direct revenue-recovery function rather than a cost center.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Quantifies the payback on failure-analysis tooling - a rare hard number for justifying FA capex and a demand argument for FA equipment vendors.
insights.quote: used dynamic laser stimulation (DLS) to localize failing transistors — recovering millions of dollars per month in shipments
insights.locator: How Dr. Lao inherited NVIDIA's laser scanning microscope

insights.claim: Laser voltage imaging was funded when a CFO signed a purchase order after seeing an image described as looking like a bloody crime scene photo, showing FA tool procurement can be driven by visual evidence rather than ROI models.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Illustrative of how quickly FA capex clears approval once defect visibility is demonstrated - a tailwind for vendors selling new imaging modalities.
insights.quote: a CFO signing a PO after seeing what looked like "a bloody crime scene photo"
insights.locator: The development of laser voltage imaging (LVI)

themes.theme: DFT-EFA pushed upstream into the foundry

insights.claim: NVIDIA's DFT-EFA (Design for Test Electronic Failure Analysis) workflow was transferred into TSMC's failure analysis lab, enabling volume fault isolation at the foundry level upstream of the fabless customer.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Deepens the NVIDIA-TSMC operational lock-in: diagnostic methodology, not just wafer volume, now binds the two - a switching cost rivals must also pay.
insights.quote: How the DFT-EFA workflow was transferred to TSMC's FA lab, enabling foundry-level volume fault isolation upstream
insights.locator: How the DFT-EFA workflow was transferred to TSMC's FA lab

insights.claim: Pattern emission microscopy is used as a bring-up checklist tool for validating DFT test patterns, tying failure analysis into the design-for-test flow rather than treating it as post-mortem debug.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Signals that FA is shifting left into bring-up, expanding the addressable window for FA tooling across the product cycle.
insights.quote: Pattern emission microscopy as a bring-up checklist tool for validating DFT test patterns
insights.locator: Pattern emission microscopy as a bring-up checklist

insights.claim: The discipline has evolved from silicon IC fault isolation to full system-level fault isolation spanning boards and complete systems, reflecting that the unit of failure is now the rack-scale system rather than the die.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms system-level diagnostics as a growing spend category as AI hardware ships as integrated systems, not chips.
insights.quote: Evolution from silicon IC fault isolation to full system-level fault isolation covering boards, systems, and everything in between
insights.locator: Evolution from silicon IC fault isolation

themes.theme: Scaling a small team against NVIDIA's growth

insights.claim: NVIDIA grew from roughly 1,000 to 36,000 employees while its failure analysis team scaled through expertise, triage and collaboration rather than proportional headcount.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A 36x headcount expansion with a non-scaling FA function implies heavy leverage on tooling and automation - the structural reason FA software and instrumentation demand outruns FA hiring.
insights.quote: NVIDIA's growth from ~1,000 to 36,000 employees — and how a small FA team scaled to meet demand through expertise, triage, and collaboration

insights.claim: Backside power delivery is named as an emerging challenge for failure analysis, because routing power from the wafer backside obstructs the optical access that laser-based fault isolation techniques depend on.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Backside power adoption at leading nodes creates a forced refresh cycle in FA tooling - watch vendors positioned for backside-compatible isolation.
insights.quote: Emerging challenges: backside power delivery, workforce development, and university-industry FA programs

insights.claim: Workforce development and university-industry FA programs are flagged alongside backside power as the field's binding constraints, indicating a talent shortage in failure analysis rather than a technology gap.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity in FA argues for automation-heavy solutions capturing the value where humans cannot be hired fast enough.
